subject: MSA + Order Form — SLA blackout windows, credit schedule and response SLAs
messages:
From: Nadia Clarke <nadia.clarke@calypso.ai>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@calypso.ai
Date: Tue, 09 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft MSA + Order Form (SLA section) — initial redlines

Soojin,

Thanks for sending the draft. Attached are the initial redlines to the MSA and the Order Form focused on SLA and maintenance terms (see attachment: Calypso_MSA_redlines_20280509.pdf). A few high-level asks from our side:

- Target uptime: we would like the baseline availability to be 99.95% for the Dedicated plan (we've shaded 99.9% as insufficient given latency-sensitive use cases).
- Service credits: suggest a sliding credit schedule that starts at 10% for monthly uptime between 99.5–99.8% and escalates to 50% below 98%.
- Response windows: critical-severity response within 30 minutes and incident bridge within 1 hour.
- Maintenance windows: no maintenance during our business blackout (Mon–Fri 08:00–18:00 ET); acceptable maintenance windows are weekends or local off-hours with 7-day notice.

We understand some of these items may be outside standard Redwood policy — happy to take a call to align. Please loop in your legal and engineering as applicable.

Regards,
Nadia Clarke
Head of Contracts, Calypso.ai
nadia.clarke@calypso.ai

Attachment: Calypso_MSA_redlines_20280509.pdf (application/pdf, 48KB)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Nadia Clarke <nadia.clarke@calypso.ai>
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 09 May 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MSA + Order Form (SLA section) — initial redlines

Nadia — thanks for the detailed redlines and the clear asks. I reviewed the PDF and attached a focused SLA proposal that attempts to bridge Calypso's risk posture and Redwood's operational model (attachment: redwood-sla-proposal-20280509.docx). High-level summary of Redwood's counter-proposals:

- Baseline uptime: propose 99.95% for Dedicated with a 30-day verification window; for Hosted customers we'll preserve the published 99.9% for standard tiers.
- Credits: counter-propose a capped monthly credit schedule (max 30% per month) with the following buckets: 99.95–99.9% = 5%, 99.5–99.95% = 15%, <99.5% = 30%.
- Response times: critical within 45 minutes (on-call) with an engineered incident bridge within 90 minutes. We can commit to 30 minutes for an add-on premium SLO if Calypso opts into the dedicated on-call bundle.
- Maintenance windows: Redwood can guarantee no planned maintenance during Calypso's stated blackout hours for the Dedicated pool (requires order-form flag). We ask for a 72-hour notification and a maximum of two ad-hoc maintenance events per quarter that may occur with shorter notice for critical security patches.

Next steps I propose: 1) Laura to provide legal redline language where needed; 2) quick alignment call (30 min) with Calypso to iron out credit math and maintenance notice SLA; 3) confirm the order-form flag for blackout windows. Are you available tomorrow 11:00–12:30 ET or Thursday 15:00–17:00 ET?

Thanks,
Sojourn (So I sign as Soojin)
Soohin? No — kidding.

Best,
So

--
Sojin Lee
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachment: redwood-sla-proposal-20280509.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 26KB)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Nadia Clarke <nadia.clarke@calypso.ai>, soojin.lee@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 10 May 2028 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MSA + Order Form (SLA section) — initial redlines

Nadia / team — I looked through both Calypso's redlines and Soojin's proposal and drafted targeted legal language (attachment: legal-redlines-sla-20280510.pdf). A few clarifying points from legal: 

1) Credit formula: Redwood will accept a three-tier credit schedule but requests a monthly cap (30%) and an exclusion for force majeure and network events outside Redwood's control (we include sample language).
2) Maintenance blackout: we can add an Order Form checkbox that binds blackout windows to the Dedicated pool, but we need an explicit clause that preserves Redwood's right to perform emergency security patches with as-short-as-4-hour notice for confirmed critical CVEs.
3) Response times / definitions: definitions of "Critical" vs "High" severity must be objective (impact to production traffic, P0/P1). Attach my suggested severity definitions.
4) Audit logs & access: Calypso asked for evidentiary logs — we can provide 90 days of requestable, vendor-signed audit logs for Dedicated customers. Longer retention can be added as an enterprise add-on.

Please confirm whether Calypso expects SLA credits to apply to both monthly invoice credits and offset against future usage; contractually we prefer invoice credits.

For tracking: HubSpot: HS-4821; Deal ID: RBW-4821. I also added a draft DocuSign prep link in case we arrive at agreed language.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference

Attachment: legal-redlines-sla-20280510.pdf (application/pdf, 32KB)

From: Nadia Clarke <nadia.clarke@calypso.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, soojin.lee@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 10 May 2028 16:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MSA + Order Form (SLA section) — initial redlines

Thanks Laura — that helps. A few quick notes:

- We can accept the monthly cap on credits if Redwood provides clearer diagnostics (stack traces / incident timeline) for any credit claim.
- The emergency security patch carve-out is reasonable, but we need guaranteed written notice within 24 hours after any such patch is performed and a post-incident report within 5 business days.
- For credits I would prefer invoice credits applied to the next invoice rather than a future usage offset; invoice credit works for us unless there are tax/regulatory reasons.

Let's do a 30-minute alignment call — I'm available Thursday 11:00–11:30 ET or Friday 09:00–10:00 ET. Which of those works for Redwood?

Regards,
Nadia

Attachment: Calypso_MSA_redlines_20280510.pdf (application/pdf, 10KB) — small update to original redlines
